points.title: SELECT query and result set
points.must: Definitions: SELECT extracts data without changing tables; result set = rows and columns returned (many, one or none).
points.model:
SELECT query = SQL statement that extracts data from tables without changing them: SELECT fields FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY field;
Result set = the table of rows and columns returned — only the chosen fields of the records that meet the condition; may have many rows, one or none.

points.title: Clauses of SELECT
points.must: SELECT (fields), FROM (table), WHERE (records), GROUP BY, ORDER BY ASC/DESC, LIMIT, in that order; SELECT = columns, WHERE = rows.
points.model: SELECT Name, Grade — which fields (* = all); FROM Student — which table; WHERE Grade = 11 — which records; GROUP BY City; ORDER BY Name ASC / DESC; LIMIT 10. SELECT chooses columns, WHERE chooses rows. Example: SELECT Name, City FROM Student WHERE Grade = 11 ORDER BY Name → Aigerim Almaty, Aruzhan Astana.

points.title: Named fields vs SELECT *
points.must: Reasons to name fields in program code; building a query with optional conditions using placeholders.
points.model: Named fields: clear code, less data sent, works if fields are added, fixes column order (needed for numeric indexes). SELECT * for quick tests. Optional filters: start WHERE 1 = 1 and add " AND Grade = ?" — values still bound.

points.title: WHERE operators
points.must: =, <>, <, >, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE with % and _, IS NULL, AND/OR/NOT; AND before OR, use brackets.
points.model: City <> 'Astana'; Grade >= 12; Grade BETWEEN 10 AND 11; City IN ('Almaty','Shymkent'); Name LIKE 'A%' (starts with A), '%ar%' (contains ar); City IS NULL. AND is evaluated before OR: WHERE (City = 'Astana' OR City = 'Almaty') AND Grade = 12 → Daniyar.

points.title: Aggregate functions and GROUP BY
points.must: Definition; COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN; GROUP BY one value per group; AS alias.
points.model: Aggregate function = calculates one value from many records: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Student WHERE City = 'Almaty' → 2. SELECT City, COUNT(*) AS Pupils FROM Student GROUP BY City → one row per city; alias read as $row["Pupils"].

points.title: Joining two tables
points.must: INNER JOIN … ON matching primary/foreign key; missing join condition pairs every row with every row.
points.model:
SELECT Student.Name, Mark.Subject, Mark.Score FROM Student INNER JOIN Mark ON Student.StudentID = Mark.StudentID WHERE Mark.Subject = 'Computer Science' ORDER BY Mark.Score DESC;
Or FROM Student, Mark WHERE Student.StudentID = Mark.StudentID. Without the join condition: 5 students × 20 marks = 100 meaningless rows.

points.title: Predicting the result of a query
points.must: Method: FROM → WHERE → GROUP → SELECT columns → ORDER BY, with a worked result.
points.model: Apply clauses in order: table → keep rows passing WHERE → group → keep SELECT columns → sort. SELECT Grade, COUNT(*) FROM Student GROUP BY Grade ORDER BY Grade DESC → 12: 2, 11: 2, 10: 1.

points.title: Running a SELECT and the fetch loop
points.must: mysqli_query returns a result object (false on error); mysqli_num_rows; while ($row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result)) runs once per row and stops at null.

points.title: Fetch functions
points.must: fetch_assoc (field names), fetch_row (numeric, SELECT order), fetch_array (both), fetch_all (all rows = 2D array).
points.model: mysqli_fetch_assoc → $row["Name"]; mysqli_fetch_row → $row[1] (index in SELECT order); mysqli_fetch_array → both; mysqli_fetch_all($result, MYSQLI_ASSOC) → all rows at once, $rows[0]["Name"]. fetch_assoc preferred: indexes do not break if the SELECT changes.

points.title: Prepared SELECT
points.must: Input in the condition needs a prepared statement: prepare, bind, execute, mysqli_stmt_get_result, then fetch loop.

points.title: Empty result vs failed query
points.must: False = SQL error; result with num_rows 0 = no match → show 'No records found'.
points.model: SQL error (wrong field, lost connection) → mysqli_query returns false → show error. Valid query, no match → result object, mysqli_num_rows = 0 → show "No pupils found". Matches → show rows.

points.title: Result set as an HTML table
points.must: Header row once before the loop, one per row inside the loop, once after; htmlspecialchars.

points.title: Search page with LIKE
points.must: GET form; % added to the bound value, not around ?; (Title LIKE ? OR Author LIKE ?) AND Copies > 0; worked result.

points.title: Details page and drop-down list
points.must: ID passed in the link, (int), WHERE StudentID = ?, one fetch without a loop; <option> per row with SELECT DISTINCT.
points.model: <a href='student.php?id=3'> → $id = (int)$_GET["id"]; SELECT * FROM Student WHERE StudentID = ? → one row or none; $row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($result); if null → "not found". Drop-down: SELECT DISTINCT City FROM Student ORDER BY City; echo "<option value='$c'>$c</option>" in the loop.

points.title: Totals in SQL or in a loop
points.must: Compare aggregate vs loop; loop algorithm for count, total, best, passed with check count > 0.
